evidence.quote: Were you approached by community and/or political party representatives?

claims.text: Per-interview record: a binary report of whether the unnamed 'you' was approached by community and/or political party representatives; no time frame is stated and the stem does not identify respondent versus interviewer as the addressee.

evidence.quote: Did you feel threatened during the interview?

claims.text: Per-interview record: a binary report of felt threat during the interview; the referent is subjective threat in the interview event, without a named threatening actor or a time beyond the interview.

evidence.quote: Were you physically threatened during the interview?

claims.text: Per-interview record: a binary report of physical threat during the interview; it records physical threat specifically, not a general security assessment.
Per-interview record: a three-position evaluation of the respondent's honesty toward the addressee during the interview; it is an attitude rating, not a factual audit of answers.

evidence.quote: The [president] must always obey the laws and the courts

claims.text: Per-interview record: forced-choice agreement between presidential non-binding and presidential obedience to laws and courts; it records a stated normative position, not observed presidential conduct.

evidence.quote: It is legitimate for the armed forces to take control of government when elected leaders abuse power

claims.text: Per-interview record: forced-choice agreement on whether military control is legitimate when elected leaders abuse power; it records a stated norm about armed forces in politics, not an event report.

evidence.quote: making sure that, once elected, [members of Parliament] do their jobs?

claims.text: Per-interview record: single-choice attribution of responsibility for ensuring elected MPs do their jobs among specified responsible actors; it is an attribution norm, not an observation of who actually monitors MPs.

evidence.quote: making sure that, once elected, the [president] does [his] job?

claims.text: Per-interview record: single-choice attribution of responsibility for ensuring the elected president does the job among specified responsible actors; it is an attribution norm, not a report of actual oversight.

evidence.quote: she will be criticized, called names, or harassed by others in the community

claims.text: Per-interview record: hypothetical likelihood that a woman in the respondent's community who runs for elected office will be criticized, called names, or harassed by community others; referent is community reaction, not the respondent's own action.

evidence.quote: should government and elected officials be doing more than they are doing now to advance the rights and equality of women

claims.text: Per-interview record: stated directional preference on whether government and elected officials should do more, less, or about the right amount on women's rights and equality; it is not a budget or policy-performance measure.

evidence.quote: which of the following issues related to women's rights and equality do you think is the most important

claims.text: Per-interview record: one most-important women's-rights issue selected from a closed list that includes none and other; it records a priority choice, not a ranking or prevalence estimate.

evidence.quote: using the police and security forces to enforce public health mandates

claims.text: Per-interview record: normative agreement that temporarily limiting democracy through police or security enforcement of public-health mandates is justified in a public-health emergency; it refers to a specified measure, not actual enforcement.

evidence.quote: Who do you think sent us to do this interview?

claims.text: Per-interview record: the respondent's belief about who sent the interview team, from closed categories including Afrobarometer or national partner, political party, government, international organization, and God; it records attributed sponsorship, not verified sponsorship.
